correctness.rationale: The nondegenerate bilinear multiplication model follows from the standard grading and one-dimensional socle. Each nonzero socle element is universal. For each nonzero degree-one vector \(v\), exactly \(q^d-1\) nonzero vertices annihilate it (self included), so deletion of loops produces degree \(q^d-2\) if and only if \(B(v,v)=0\), and \(q^d-1\) otherwise. Counting finite-field quadratic zeros (odd \(q\) via Gauss sums; even \(q\) via the square of a linear functional) gives the stated multiset. Standard classification of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms by similarity implies isotropic count determines the ring type, even in characteristic two. The 13 standalone prime-field enumerations reproduced exact degree frequencies, and the general argument does not depend on those finite runs.

originality.rationale: The full ordinary simple zero-divisor graph degree multiset yields all ring-isomorphism invariants in the natural standard graded Hilbert-\((1,d,1)\) Gorenstein family. The 2020 Kadu bilinear orthogonality premise and classical finite-field form classification are explicitly prior and not counted as new. A 2026 Kadu–Tanpure paper concerns a compressed-graph Gorenstein test; 2020 Lao et al. calculate graph degrees for a fixed degenerate multiplication, and 2024 Ndago et al. cover a distinct large square layer. No equivalent all-field degree-sequence reconstruction theorem emerged from primary-text and published research-record comparisons; historical implicit synthesis remains possible.
residual_risks: Another published result may formulate the same reconstruction as a corollary of bilinear-space orthogonality and finite-field quadratic-form classification.
Chiteng’a 2005 cube-radical-zero ring classification was accessible in abstract but not fully compared; ring classification itself is not claimed new.
The 2024 primary PDF was inspected for scope and construction, rather than exhaustively checking each later proposition; its explicit dimension restriction separates its studied rings.

value.rationale: General zero-divisor graphs do not determine their rings, so complete recovery from mere vertex degrees on a canonical infinite local Gorenstein family is a motivated rigidity phenomenon. The precise \(q\)- and dimension-uniform formula exposes the otherwise hidden even-dimensional discriminant or characteristic-two alternating invariant. It is not a small-table recomputation; the result covers every prime-power finite field and every embedding dimension at least two, while carefully separating borrowed bilinear and form-classification lemmas from the new graph reconstruction.
